chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Aban from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Prayer over the dead is disliked when the sun yellows and when it rises."

Thus, this report is explicit regarding dislike (karahah) rather than prohibition (hadr), and it is possible that the reason for this dislike in this matter is that it was the practice of some of the Sunnis, so it was presented as an act of precaution (taqiyyah).

key_terms.اَلْعَامَّةِ: the general public (often referring to Sunnis in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying over the dead during sunrise and sunset in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the makruh (disliked) status of funeral prayers during the specific times of sun rise (ishraq) and sun yellowing (istiwaa), distinguishing it from strict prohibition (haram). The commentator suggests this ruling may stem from taqiyyah, reflecting a cautious alignment with the prevailing practices of the Sunni majority to avoid unnecessary conflict. This highlights the nuanced approach of Shia jurisprudence in balancing ritual purity with social harmony.
